Despite the brevity of the script, both central characters—Lukas and Anna—are developed with an appropriate level of complexity that makes them feel like real people rather than mere plot devices. Through subtext, body language (Anna keeping her coat on, Lukas twisting his wedding ring), and sharp dialogue, the reader quickly understands their distinct personalities, their shared history, and their conflicting coping mechanisms. Lukas clings to the past to a fault (creating an environment where there is "no room to breathe"), while Anna avoids confrontation and tries to sever ties completely. Neither character is portrayed as purely right or wrong; they both display vulnerabilities, bitterness, and emotional depth. The only other character mentioned onstage is the waitress, a background figure whose brief appearance is used naturally to pace the scene and emphasize the awkward silence between the former couple, which is entirely appropriate for her role.
